notes: Identity verified from the supplied document: title Superior facial emotion recognition in adolescents with anorexia nervosa – A replication study; Anca Sfärlea, Christina Buhl, Linda Lukas, Gerd Schulte‐Körne; DOI 10.1002/erv.3103; European Eating Disorders Review 2024, 32:943–951. This is a full primary brief report (abstract, methods, results, discussion, references), not an abstract-only parse. No PDF is assigned. The Supplement is referenced but is not contained in the supplied source. Emotion-identification description does not specify the response measure, ANOVA term or emotion contrast. Even restricting to accuracy, multiple printed model terms and afraid/sad contrasts remain. Requested metric alone does not uniquely identify the target. Accuracy omnibus candidates: TASK F1,72=23.05, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.243; EMOTION F3.60,259.32=87.04, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.547; TASK × GROUP F1,72=7.55, p=0.008, partial eta-squared=0.095; TASK × EMOTION F3.53,254.47=42.12, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.369; three-way interaction F3.53,254.47=3.08, p=0.021, partial eta-squared=0.041. GROUP and EMOTION × GROUP collectively Fs≤1.50, ps>0.1. Emotion-task follow-ups: EMOTION F3.33,239.86=72.19, p<0.001, partial eta-squared=0.501; GROUP F1,72=4.59, p=0.036, partial eta-squared=0.060; EMOTION × GROUP F3.33,239.86=2.79, p=0.036, partial eta-squared=0.037. Pairwise afraid t67.97=2.66, p=0.010, d=0.59; sad t72=2.20, p=0.031, d=0.51 (not significant after correction). Other emotions collectively ts≤1.54, ps>0.1. These are separate candidate tests, not mapped by input order. Candidate common main-report analytic sample: 33 AN + 41 HC = 74 adolescent participants in mutually exclusive included groups; not derived from degrees of freedom. Main report describes the mixed TASK × EMOTION × GROUP ANOVAs and no additional participant exclusions for those reported models. Eligibility excludes IQ <85, visual impairments, specified neurological/psychiatric disorders and substance abuse; HC excludes current/past mental disorders. Endnote 2 describes a separate sensitivity analysis excluding two AN participants above the 10th BMI percentile; this is not substituted for the main analysis. Model sample cannot be assigned to an unidentified row-specific test; retain only as a candidate. Misclassification model inclusion/exclusions cannot be verified without Supplement. Authors explicitly describe successful replication at whole-study level; reported_success preserves that narrative verdict only, not a claim of a uniquely identified row-specific test. The neutral description mentions major depression; the replication actually compares AN with HC, with depression sometimes comorbid within AN, not a separate major-depression group. No mapping is inferred from row order, original statistics or numeric agreement.
